newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on technical selloff.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on technical selloff.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended lower Thursday in a moderately active session, with technical selling after an early rally stalled undermining the complex despite reports of firmer cash.
June slumped 8.1 cents to close at $2.195 per million British thermal units. July settled 7.5 cents lower at $2.20. Most other deferreds ended down by 0.8 to 6.5 cents.
"When June failed to break above $2.30 it prompted some technical selling and liquidation, but I don't know if we're going to break down much further unless cash comes off," said one Midwest trader.
Technical traders said June may be range-bound, with support in the $2.15 area and resistance at $2.30. Major buying was likely at $2.05. The contract high is $2.43.
While cash seems relatively well-supported by steady injections and some Southwest heat, few expected a break to new highs until broader cooling loads kick in.
Weather next week in the Southeast was expected to warm to slightly above-normal, but seasonal to slightly-below seasonal temperatures were forecast for the Midwest and Northeast.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices gained a few cents Thursday to the low-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the $2.03-2.08 area. New York city gate gas also was up slightly in the high-$2.40s.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line, which began Saturday, will continue to cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd through Monday, with 400 mmcfd still cut May 20-22.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip slipped 4.9 cents to $2.234. NYMEX said 41,281 contracts traded, up from Wednesday's revised tally of 34,058.

On the KCBT, June finished 4.2 cents lower at $2.058, while deferreds ended down by 3.5 to 4.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 3.9 cents to 13.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 445 contracts traded, down from Wednesday's total of 285.
